b.203f5bcb66:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>E</c>xsúltet cælum láudibus,
Resúltet terra gáudiis:
Apostolórum glóriam
Sacra canunt solémnia.

<h>V</h>os sæcli iusti iúdices,
Et vera mundi lúmina,
Votis precámur córdium,
Audíte preces súpplicum.

<h>Q</h>ui cælum verbo cláuditis,
Serásque eius sólvitis:
Nos a peccátis ómnibus
Sólvite iussu, quǽsumus.

<h>Q</h>uorum præcépto súbditur,
Salus, et languor ómnium:
Sanáte ægros móribus,
Nos reddéntes virtútibus.

<h>U</h>t, cum Iudex advénerit
Christus in fine sǽculi,
Nos sempitérni gáudii
Fáciat esse cómpotes.

<h>D</h>eo Patri sit glória,
Eiúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Et nunc, et in perpétuum.
Amen.
b.d19229cdde:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>N</c>ow let the earth with joy resound,
And heaven the chant re-echo round;
Nor heaven nor earth too high can raise
The great Apostles' glorious praise.

<h>O</h> ye who, throned in glory dread,
Shall judge the living and the dead,
Lights of the world forevermore!
To you the suppliant prayer we pour.

<h>Y</h>e close the sacred gates on high;
At your command apart they fly:
Oh! loose for us the guilty chain
We strive to break, and strive in vain.

<h>S</h>ickness and health your voice obey;
At your command they go or stay:
From sin's disease our souls restore;
In good confirm us more and more.

<h>S</h>o when the world is at its end,
And Christ to judgement shall descend,
May we be called those joys to see
Prepared from all eternity.

<h>P</h>raise to the Father, with the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One;
As ever was in ages past,
And so shall be while ages last.
Amen.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Actibus Apostolórum
<r>Act 3:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> Petrus autem et Ioánnes ascendébant in templum ad horam oratiónis nonam.
<n>2</n> Et quidam vir, qui erat claudus ex útero matris suæ, baiulabátur; quem ponébant cotídie ad portam templi, quæ dícitur Speciósa, ut péteret eleemósynam ab introëúntibus in templum.
<n>3</n> Is, cum vidísset Petrum et Ioánnem incipiéntes introíre in templum, rogábat ut eleemósynam accíperet.
<n>4</n> Intuens autem in eum Petrus cum Ioánne, dixit: Réspice in nos.
<n>5</n> At ille intendébat in eos, sperans se áliquid acceptúrum ab eis.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Simon Petre, ántequam de navi vocárem te, novi te et super plebem meam príncipem te constítui:
* Et claves regni cælórum trádidi tibi.
<r>℣.</r> Quodcúmque ligáveris super terram erit ligátum et in cælis; et quodcúmque sólveris super terram, erit solútum et in cælis.
<r>℟.</r> Et claves regni cælórum trádidi tibi.

<r>Acts 3:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> Now Peter and John went up into the temple at the ninth hour of prayer.
<n>2</n> And a certain man who was lame from his mother's womb, was carried: whom they laid every day at the gate of the temple, which is called Beautiful, that he might ask alms of them that went into the temple.
<n>3</n> He, when he had seen Peter and John about to go into the temple, asked to receive an alms.
<n>4</n> But Peter with John fastening his eyes upon him, said: Look upon us.
<n>5</n> But he looked earnestly upon them, hoping that he should receive something of them.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Simon Peter, before I called thee out of the ship, I knew thee, and appointed thee for a ruler over My people.
* And I have given unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
<r>℣.</r> Whatsoever, thou shalt bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven; and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven.
<r>℟.</r> And I have given unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven.

<n>10</n> Cognoscébant autem illum, quod ipse erat, qui ad eleemósynam sedébat ad Speciósam portam templi; et impléti sunt stupóre et éxtasi in eo, quod contígerat illi.
